ambiguities.issue: The effective-window denominator may be zero.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (2.24) divides c by max_i ||X_i||_psi1, but the inherited hypotheses permit all X_i to have psi-one norm zero and the passage gives no assumption that this maximum is positive.
ambiguities.impact: In ordinary real analysis the displayed quotient is undefined when the maximum is zero. An exact formalization must not silently choose among adding a positive-maximum hypothesis, treating the radius as infinity, using a totalized division convention that makes c/0 a finite value such as zero, or splitting off the degenerate family.

ambiguities.issue: The exact numerical values and identity of c and C are not fixed.
ambiguities.evidence: The passage calls c an absolute constant in the enclosing theorem, uses C in the MGF estimate, and footnote 8 specifies only comparability up to an absolute factor.
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement may quantify suitable positive absolute constants, but it cannot extract exact numerical constants or assume that identically lettered constants elsewhere are definitionally the same without an additional convention.

ambiguities.issue: The source does not explicitly state the degenerate conclusion when every psi-one norm is zero.
ambiguities.evidence: No separate all-zero case accompanies Equation (2.24), despite the zero denominator.
ambiguities.impact: Although zero psi-one norm conventionally forces the variables to vanish almost surely and would make the MGF bound trivial for every lambda, that repair is analyst inference rather than an explicit part of the selected passage.

contract_plain_english: For each member X_i of a finite independent family of mean-zero sub-exponential random variables, the source gives a common effective MGF window determined by the largest psi-one norm in the family. If the real parameter lambda satisfies |lambda| <= c/max_j ||X_j||_psi1, then E exp(lambda X_i) <= exp(C lambda^2 ||X_i||_psi1^2). Here c and C are unspecified positive absolute constants, and footnote 8 supplies only absolute-factor comparison between the property-e scale and the psi-one norm. The passage does not say what the quotient means when every psi-one norm is zero, so that case must remain explicitly ambiguous rather than being resolved by an unstated division convention.
